sections.title: Sound of á
paragraphs: The letter name is (á) /a/. Its main sound is a vowel, heard in the word (água) /ˈa.ɡwɐ/, which means water. A vowel is a sound made with open air and no touch in the mouth. This letter makes three sounds.

sections.title: How to say it
paragraphs: For the first sound, relax your tongue in the centre of your mouth and open your mouth slightly. For the second sound, drop your jaw low and keep your tongue flat at the bottom. For the third sound, raise the back of your tongue toward the roof of your mouth and let air escape through your nose. Place a finger under your nose to feel warm air flow out.

sections.title: When each sound occurs
paragraphs: In unstressed syllables or before nasal consonants, it sounds like (amigo) /ɐˈmi.ɡu/ or (cama) /ˈkɐ.mɐ/. In stressed syllables, you hear the open sound as in (pá) /pa/. With an accent mark like a tilde or before a syllable-final nasal consonant, it becomes a nasal vowel, heard in (mãe) /mɐ̃j̃/ and (canto) /ˈkɐ̃.tu/.

sections.title: Mistakes to avoid
paragraphs: Do not replace the unstressed sound with the bright vowel in cat. Keep your mouth smaller and your tongue central, closer to the vowel in cup. Do not pronounce the final nasal consonant in words like (canto) /ˈkɐ̃.tu/. Never say a full n sound at the end of that syllable.
